subproblems.title: Every vector Dψ(v)a is the velocity of a C¹ curve in N
subproblems.statement: Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ with r ≥ 1, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d open, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P of class C^r on V with ψ(V) ⊆ N. Then for every v ∈ V, Dψ(v)(ℝ^d) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)), where Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v. Here tangentSpace N y is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and satisfies γ(0) = y and γ'(0) = w (HasDerivAt γ w 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P r d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ N → ∀ v ∈ V, Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Extracted from step 2 of the supplied proof (with the reparametrisation made explicit).
1. Setup. Since r ≥ 1, ψ is C¹ on V (a C^r map is C^k on V for every k ≤ r). As V is open and v ∈ V, V is a neighbourhood of v, so ψ is differentiable at v; write L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v, so HasFDerivAt ψ L v.
2. Let w ∈ range L, say w = L a with a ∈ ℝ^d. We produce a curve γ witnessing w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)).
3. Case a = 0. Then w = L 0 = 0. Take the constant curve γ(t) := ψ(v). It is smooth, hence C¹ on (−1, 1); its values equal ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N, so it maps (−1, 1) into N; γ(0) = ψ(v); and its derivative at 0 is 0 = w. Hence w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)). (This case also covers d = 0, where a = 0 always.)
4. Case a ≠ 0, so |a| > 0. Since V is open and v ∈ V, choose ρ₀ > 0 with the open ball B(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V. Put c := ρ₀/|a| > 0 and h(t) := t / (1 + t²/c²) for t ∈ ℝ. The denominator satisfies 1 + t²/c² ≥ 1 > 0, so h is smooth on ℝ (a quotient of smooth functions with nonvanishing denominator), in particular C¹. We have h(0) = 0, and by the quotient rule h'(t) = ((1 + t²/c²) − t·(2t/c²)) / (1 + t²/c²)², so h'(0) = 1. Moreover |h(t)| ≤ c/2 for all t: since (c − |t|)² ≥ 0 we get 2c|t| ≤ c² + t², i.e. |t| ≤ (c/2)(1 + t²/c²), and dividing by the positive denominator gives |h(t)| ≤ c/2. (h plays the role of the reparametrisation σ(s) = κ·tanh(s/κ) of the supplied proof: only smoothness, σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and boundedness are used; the rational h is chosen because the pinned Mathlib has no derivative lemmas for tanh.)
5. Define β(t) := v + h(t)·a for t ∈ ℝ. Then |β(t) − v| = |h(t)|·|a| ≤ (c/2)|a| = ρ₀/2 < ρ₀, so β(t) ∈ B(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V for every t ∈ ℝ. β is C¹ on ℝ (a constant plus a C¹ scalar function times a fixed vector), β(0) = v + 0·a = v, and β has derivative h'(0)·a = a at 0.
6. Define γ := ψ ∘ β. Since β is C¹ on ℝ, maps ℝ (in particular (−1, 1)) into V, and ψ is C¹ on V, the composition γ is C¹ on (−1, 1). For every t, γ(t) = ψ(β(t)) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N, so γ maps (−1, 1) into N. Also γ(0) = ψ(β(0)) = ψ(v).
7. Chain rule: ψ has Fréchet derivative L at β(0) = v and β has derivative a at 0, hence γ = ψ ∘ β has derivative L(a) = w at 0.
8. By steps 6–7, γ witnesses w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)). Since w ∈ range L was arbitrary (steps 3 and 4–7 cover both cases), Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v).
proof_key_steps: r ≥ 1 and V open give ψ ∈ C¹(V) and HasFDerivAt ψ (fderiv ℝ ψ v) v.
For w = L a with a = 0 the constant curve ψ(v) is a witness.
For a ≠ 0 the bounded smooth reparametrisation h(t) = t/(1 + t²/c²), c = ρ₀/|a|, keeps β(t) = v + h(t)a inside B(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V, with β(0) = v, β'(0) = a.
γ = ψ ∘ β is C¹ on (−1, 1), lies in ψ(V) ⊆ N, starts at ψ(v), and has velocity L a = w by the chain rule.

subproblems.title: Continuity of the inverse of a proper injective chart (Simon Ch. 2, (4.1)–(4.2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) ⊆ W, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every v ∈ V and ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Distances are Euclidean. No openness of V or W is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ W → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → ∀ v ∈ V, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Extracted from step 3 of the supplied proof (the embedding property), stated in ε–δ form; this is the continuity of ψ⁻¹ at ψ(v) along ψ(V) used in step 4.
1. Fix v ∈ V and ε > 0, and suppose, for contradiction, that no δ > 0 works: for every δ > 0 there is v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ and |v' − v| ≥ ε.
2. Applying this with δ = 1/(j + 1) for each j ∈ ℕ, choose u_j ∈ V with |ψ(u_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j + 1) and |u_j − v| ≥ ε. Since 0 ≤ |ψ(u_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j + 1) → 0, we have ψ(u_j) → ψ(v) as j → ∞.
3. Let K := {ψ(v)} ∪ {ψ(u_j) : j ∈ ℕ}. The range of a convergent sequence together with its limit is compact, so K is compact. Since v ∈ V and every u_j ∈ V, K ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ W. By the properness hypothesis, C := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact, and every u_j lies in C (u_j ∈ V and ψ(u_j) ∈ K).
4. C is a compact subset of the metric space ℝ^d, hence sequentially compact: there are z ∈ C and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with u_{φ(i)} → z as i → ∞. In particular z ∈ V.
5. ψ is continuous on V at z ∈ V, and u_{φ(i)} ∈ V with u_{φ(i)} → z, so ψ(u_{φ(i)}) → ψ(z). On the other hand ψ(u_{φ(i)}) → ψ(v), being a subsequence of the sequence of step 2. Limits in ℝ^P are unique, so ψ(z) = ψ(v). As z, v ∈ V and ψ is injective on V, z = v.
6. Hence u_{φ(i)} → v, so for some index i₀ we have |u_{φ(i₀)} − v| < ε, contradicting |u_j − v| ≥ ε for every j (step 2). Therefore some δ > 0 has the required property: every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε.
proof_key_steps: Assume the conclusion fails and pick u_j ∈ V with |ψ(u_j) − ψ(v)| < 1/(j+1) and |u_j − v| ≥ ε.
K = {ψ(v)} ∪ {ψ(u_j)} is compact and contained in ψ(V) ⊆ W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact and contains every u_j.
A subsequence converges to some z ∈ V; continuity on V and uniqueness of limits give ψ(z) = ψ(v), so z = v by injectivity.
Then u_{φ(i)} → v contradicts |u_j − v| ≥ ε.

subproblems.title: Secant estimate at a chart point from differentiability, an injective derivative and inverse continuity
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P a continuous linear map, and v ∈ V. Assume ψ(V) = W ∩ N, ψ is Fréchet differentiable at v with derivative A, and A is injective. Assume also the inverse-continuity condition at v: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ satisfies |v' − v| < ε. Then for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − ψ(v)| < δ admits some a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − ψ(v) − Aa| ≤ ε|y − ψ(v)|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (A : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), IsOpen W → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → v ∈ V → HasFDerivAt ψ A v → Injective A → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ v' ∈ V, dist (ψ v') (ψ v) < δ → dist v' v < ε) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y (ψ v) < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - ψ v - A a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - ψ v‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Extracted from steps 1, 4 and 5 of the supplied proof: the lift of points of N near ψ(v) through ψ (step 4), the coercivity of L = Dψ(v) (step 1) and the remainder absorption (step 5), applied to an arbitrary point y = ψ(v') of N near ψ(v) instead of the points γ(s) of a curve.
1. Coercivity (supplied step 1). A is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^d, so it is bounded below: there is K > 0 with |h| ≤ K|A h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d (equivalently |A h| ≥ c|h| with c = 1/K; an injective linear map from a finite-dimensional normed space is antilipschitz). If d = 0 every h is 0 and any K > 0 works.
2. Fix ε > 0. Put m := min(1, ε) > 0 and η := m/(2K) > 0; then K·η = m/2 ≤ 1/2.
3. Remainder bound (supplied step 5). Since ψ has Fréchet derivative A at v, ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v) = o(|v' − v|) as v' → v; hence there is ρ > 0 such that |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| for all v' ∈ ℝ^d with |v' − v| < ρ.
4. Choice of δ. By the inverse-continuity hypothesis applied with ρ > 0, there is δ₁ > 0 such that every v' ∈ V with |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ₁ satisfies |v' − v| < ρ. Since v ∈ V, ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N ⊆ W, and W is open, so there is δ₂ > 0 with B(ψ(v), δ₂) ⊆ W. Put δ := min(δ₁, δ₂) > 0.
5. Lift (supplied step 4). Let y ∈ N with |y − ψ(v)| < δ. Then |y − ψ(v)| < δ₂, so y ∈ W; hence y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), i.e. y = ψ(v') for some v' ∈ V. Since |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| < δ₁, step 4 gives |v' − v| < ρ, and step 3 gives |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v|.
6. Absorption (supplied step 5). By the triangle inequality, |A(v' − v)| ≤ |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| + |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ |ψ(v') − ψ(v)| + η|v' − v|. Multiplying by K and using step 1, |v' − v| ≤ K|A(v' − v)| ≤ K|ψ(v') − ψ(v)| + Kη|v' − v| ≤ K|ψ(v') − ψ(v)| + (1/2)|v' − v|, hence |v' − v| ≤ 2K|ψ(v') − ψ(v)|.
7. Conclusion. Take a := v' − v. Then |y − ψ(v) − A a| = |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| ≤ η·2K|ψ(v') − ψ(v)| = m|y − ψ(v)| ≤ ε|y − ψ(v)|, using 2Kη = m ≤ ε. So δ has the required property.
proof_key_steps: Injective A on finite-dimensional ℝ^d is bounded below: |h| ≤ K|Ah|.
Differentiability gives |ψ(v') − ψ(v) − A(v' − v)| ≤ η|v' − v| for |v' − v| < ρ, with η = min(1, ε)/(2K).
Inverse continuity and openness of W give δ such that y ∈ N, |y − ψ(v)| < δ forces y = ψ(v'), v' ∈ V, |v' − v| < ρ.
Absorbing the remainder gives |v' − v| ≤ 2K|y − ψ(v)|, so a = v' − v satisfies |y − ψ(v) − Aa| ≤ ε|y − ψ(v)|.

subproblems.title: Under a secant estimate, curve velocities lie in the range of A
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P, q ∈ ℝ^P, and A : ℝ^d → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. Assume that for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every y ∈ N with |y − q| < δ admits some a ∈ ℝ^d with |y − q − Aa| ≤ ε|y − q|. Then tangentSpace N q ⊆ A(ℝ^d). Here tangentSpace N q is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and satisfies γ(0) = q and γ'(0) = w (HasDerivAt γ w 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (q : Euclid P) (A : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P), (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ N, dist y q < δ → ∃ a : Euclid d, ‖y - q - A a‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - q‖) → tangentSpace N q ⊆ Set.range A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Extracted from step 6 of the supplied proof: the difference quotients of a curve in N lie within o(1) of range L, and range L is closed.
1. Let w ∈ tangentSpace N q, witnessed by γ : ℝ → ℝ^P with γ(t) ∈ N for t ∈ (−1, 1), γ(0) = q and HasDerivAt γ w 0. (The C¹ property of γ is not needed.)
2. L := A(ℝ^d) is a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, hence closed; it is nonempty (0 = A0 ∈ L). For x ∈ ℝ^P let dist(x, L) := inf{|x − ℓ| : ℓ ∈ L}; this function is continuous (1-Lipschitz) and nonnegative, and for the closed nonempty set L, dist(x, L) = 0 iff x ∈ L.
3. For t ≠ 0 let s(t) := t⁻¹(γ(t) − q) = t⁻¹(γ(t) − γ(0)) be the difference quotient. Since HasDerivAt γ w 0, s(t) → w as t → 0 with t ≠ 0 (along the punctured neighbourhood filter of 0, which is nontrivial).
4. Claim: dist(w, L) ≤ ε|w| for every ε > 0. Fix ε > 0 and take δ > 0 from the hypothesis. γ is continuous at 0 (it is differentiable there) and γ(0) = q, so |γ(t) − q| < δ for all t near 0; also t ∈ (−1, 1) for t near 0, and then γ(t) ∈ N. For such t with t ≠ 0, the hypothesis at y = γ(t) gives a ∈ ℝ^d with |γ(t) − q − A a| ≤ ε|γ(t) − q|. Since A(t⁻¹a) ∈ L and A is linear, dist(s(t), L) ≤ |s(t) − A(t⁻¹a)| = |t⁻¹|·|γ(t) − q − A a| ≤ |t⁻¹|·ε|γ(t) − q| = ε|s(t)|. Thus dist(s(t), L) ≤ ε|s(t)| for all t ≠ 0 near 0.
